note: Findings Eve made on real pull requests, with what is actually true of the code at that commit. truth: false = the claim is wrong (the checks should not show it); true = a real defect, at most max_priority; overstated = the fact is right but the severity is not, so showing it above max_priority is wrong (hiding it is fine). See README.md.

findings.title: Window calculation can overflow for a huge window_minutes
findings.impact: window := int64(ru.WindowMinutes) * 60_000 overflows if WindowMinutes is very large (user-controlled).
findings.why: validRule in api/alerts.go caps the window at 7 days; that is in another file, so the check must say unclear, not guess.

findings.title: CountSourceEvents filters on source_id and timestamp without a composite index
findings.impact: Queries filtering by source_id and timestamp across daily shards do full scans as event volume grows.
findings.why: idx_events_source (source_id, timestamp DESC) exists in the day file schema in pkg/storage/days.go, another file.

findings.title: checkVolume runs without the engine mutex
findings.impact: If Check() runs concurrently, two invocations may process the same rule and create duplicate alerts.
findings.evidence: func (e *Engine) checkVolume(ctx context.Context, rules []storage.Rule, now int64, res *Result) {
findings.why: checkVolume is only called from Check, which takes e.mu on its first line and holds it to the end (same file).

findings.title: fillSources silently changes which source a volume rule watches when its source was deleted
findings.impact: If the rule's source was deleted, the select becomes empty and the next line picks the first source.
findings.why: A source can't be deleted while a rule watches it (DeleteSource refuses), so the case can't happen; that is in storage code, another file.

findings.title: SaveRule does not clear the search and grouping of a volume rule
findings.impact: validRule clears Query, MinSeverity, ThreatOnly and GroupBy for volume rules but SaveRule does not, so a caller that skips validRule could store them.
findings.evidence:
ru.ID == 0 {
		res, err = r.db.Write.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO alert_rules
findings.why: A real, small defense-in-depth gap at that commit (fixed later). Worth a warning, not a blocker.

findings.title: validRule accepts a threshold or window of 0
findings.impact: For volume_under with threshold 0 the condition is always true, so the rule never alerts.
findings.why: validRule rejects ru.Threshold < 1 and ru.WindowMinutes < 1 at its top, in the same function.

findings.title: SQL injection from extra-field names in condSQL
findings.impact: Malicious parser input could inject SQL through field names.
findings.why: The name goes into a bound parameter (a JSON path), never into the SQL text.

findings.title: Race condition corrupts pagination offset in showMore
findings.impact: If a new search starts while showMore is running, offset is incremented prematurely.
findings.why: The offset update is after `if (seq !== searchSeq) return;`, so an older answer is dropped first.

findings.title: fields_text value order differs from json_tree's, breaking search consistency
findings.impact: Events migrated with json_tree get a different value order than events indexed in Go, breaking search for multi-value fields.
findings.why: Stored JSON is written with sorted keys, so json_tree reads in the same order; and word order does not affect a normal full-text search.

findings.title: Missing source_id index in the day schema
findings.impact: Queries filtering by source= do full table scans on large day files.
findings.why: `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_source ON events(source_id, timestamp DESC)` is in the same schema list.

findings.title: List values stored as JSON text are not matched by a field term
findings.impact: json_type reports 'text' for a list stored as JSON text, so field="A" never matches an item.
findings.why: json_type of a text value that holds JSON text reads the JSON, so it is 'array'; a test proves it.

findings.title: Migration fails to drop the old FTS table and trigger
findings.impact: With IF NOT EXISTS the old index and trigger remain, so day files are never truly upgraded.
findings.evidence: stmts = append(stmts, ftsTable, ftsDeleteTrigger, `INSERT INTO events_fts(events_fts) VALUES ('rebuild')`)
findings.why: migrateDay starts its statement list with DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS events_ai, DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS events_ad and DROP TABLE IF EXISTS events_fts.

findings.title: splitTokens keeps the quote characters in tokens
findings.impact: The quotes are unnecessary and could interfere with how the full-text search reads the final query.
findings.why: The words left over go to the full-text search, which needs the quotes for exact phrases such as "invalid user".

findings.title: JSON path construction lacks robust escaping
findings.impact: Relying only on a regex for the safety of the JSON path is brittle if the regex changes.
findings.why: The name is checked against fieldNameRe first, passed as a bound parameter, and the regex allows no quote.

findings.title: AND token dropping is asymmetric
findings.impact: Intermediate ANDs may survive when they should be absorbed, giving unexpected search logic.
findings.why: Every neighbouring-AND case is handled and tested; dropping both neighbours would give the same search.

findings.title: TOCTOU race in tighten() allows chmod of an attacker-controlled target
findings.impact: An attacker who replaces the target with a symlink between Lstat and Open makes the fix chmod the link's target.
findings.why: It fstats the opened file and refuses unless os.SameFile matches the Lstat, then chmods the descriptor.

findings.title: Typo in the SSH PermitEmptyPasswords key makes the check miss the directive
findings.impact: The check uses permitemptypasswords instead of PermitEmptyPasswords, so a server that allows empty passwords reports Pass.
findings.why: sshdConfig lowercases every key (strings.ToLower(f[0])), and sshd keywords are case-insensitive.

findings.title: Shallow copy of SecConfig shares the SyslogAllow slice with the live config
findings.impact: Future code that appends to cfg.SyslogAllow would mutate the server's configuration across requests.
findings.evidence: cfg := s.deps.SecConfig // a copy: the counts below are per run
findings.why: True that the slice header is shared, but nothing appends to it; hypothetical.

findings.title: checkKernel reads /proc/sys inside containers without container detection
findings.impact: In a container the network settings describe the container's namespace, not the host, so Pass or Warn can mislead.
findings.why: The seven sibling host checks call hostSkip() for containers and this one does not.

findings.title: checkPorts omits SIEMLite's HTTPS port from the expected ports
findings.impact: e.Cfg.Addr is the plain HTTP address, so the HTTPS port (8443) is flagged as unexpected on every fresh install.
findings.evidence: for _, a := range []string{e.Cfg.Addr, e.Cfg.HTTPAddr, e.Cfg.SyslogUDP, e.Cfg.SyslogTCP, e.Cfg.SyslogTLS} {
findings.why: main.go sets Addr from the -addr flag, which is the HTTPS listen address. What Addr means is in another file, so the check must say unclear, not guess.

findings.title: Test references a State.History field that does not exist
findings.impact: The test will not compile because secaudit.State has no History field.
findings.why: State.History is defined in pkg/secaudit/service.go, another file, and the Tests check compiles it.

findings.title: Fail-open uid/gid parsing defaults to root on error
findings.impact: If strconv.ParseUint fails, uid and gid become 0, so the command runs as root and files are chowned to root: a privilege escalation.
findings.why: The errors really are ignored, but the installer already runs as root, so nothing is escalated; the realistic effect is a root-owned database the service cannot open.

findings.title: inContainer ignores a read error on /proc/1/cgroup
findings.impact: If the file is unreadable the function returns false and may miss a container environment.
findings.why: True, but /.dockerenv and /run/.containerenv are checked first, and the effect is a refused or failed install.

findings.title: runAs drops supplementary groups
findings.impact: The service user may need supplementary groups (docker, shared logs), which the admin-creation command lacks.
findings.why: True, but the service user is created by the installer a moment earlier and has no supplementary groups; dropping the caller's groups is the safer behaviour.

findings.title: chownTo follows symlinks (TOCTOU risk)
findings.impact: If DataDir is replaced with a symlink between MkdirAll and Chown, root could chown an arbitrary target.
findings.why: True that os.Chown follows links, but swapping DataDir needs write access to a root-owned parent such as /var/lib.
